Guardrails per channel±30% of each channel's share (Meridian default)

Google Meridian's default spend constraint: share = new budget × the channel's share of the reference budget; allowed range = 70%–130% of that share. The limits move with the budget, so every budget from Rp0 to Rp10B/month is optimized and spent in full, within the spend levels the model data cover. The table above shows each channel's allowed range at the scenario budget. Cuts deeper than −30% per platform should be phased over several periods.

02 · Diminishing Return

Return on the next rupiah by channel

Response curves estimated by Google Meridian. Solid line = incremental revenue per month. Dashed line = average iROAS. The box is the allowed range for the scenario budget (Meridian default: ±30% of the channel's share); the planner picks the point inside it that gives the most total revenue, by moving money to the channels with the highest return on the next Rp1 (mROI).

Incremental revenue / month iROAS (right axis) Allowed range (±30% of share, Meridian default) Peak iROAS (channel alone) Current budget Scenario budget (from planner) Break-even: next Rp1 returns Rp1 (mROI = 1) Loss zone: next Rp1 returns less than Rp1 Beyond model data (spend level not seen in the training data)

Channel efficiency summary

Observed vs incremental return

Observed ROAS comes from Campaign Performance (platform-reported revenue). iROAS comes from the Google Meridian model (revenue that would not happen without the media). Incremental share = iROAS ÷ Observed ROAS.

03 · Pause Planner

If a channel pauses, what is saved and what is lost?

Media effect fades after a channel stops (carryover). The pause is evaluated at the channel's scenario budget and compared with the KPI decline the business can accept.

Carryover decay

KPI decline by pause length

Drop in total revenue during the pause. The dashed line is the allowed decline; bars above it break the limit.

Assumes the channel was running at full effect before the pause; seasonality and payday peaks are not modeled. Recovery after restart takes roughly two half-lives.
